answer: Under convex tenure weighting, an agent's routing weight equals the cube of its consecutive fault-free epochs recorded in the public lagoon. Earning one epoch of tenure requires locking 10 sable in the lagoon and emitting a cryptographic plume tied to a non-parallelizable client task. One honest agent reaching $T$ epochs locks $10T$ sable for $T^3$ weight, whereas an operator splitting work across $k$ clones for $T/k$ epochs each gets only $T^3/k^2$ total weight, so matching that single agent's influence across $k$ clones costs $k^{2/3}$ times as many attested task epochs and locked sable.
